iron.description: The most common construction metal. Used in everything from the base's skeleton to hand tools. Abundantly found on the surface.

copper.description: A highly conductive, easy-to-work metal. The basic raw material for cables and electronic systems.

aluminum.description: Lightweight and durable. Preferred in transport systems, tanks, and ship hulls. Mined at medium depths.

titanium.description: A rare metal with an extraordinary strength-to-weight ratio. Essential for pressure doors and advanced technology equipment. Found in deep layers.

nickel.description: A corrosion-resistant alloy metal. Greatly increases durability when combined with titanium and iron.

chromium.description: Used for surface coating and corrosion prevention. Forms a protective layer on equipment exposed to radiation.

lithium.description: An element with high energy density. Unstable in its raw form; a damaged lithium cell can cause a fire. Indispensable for battery systems.

carbon.description: A versatile element. Traps impurities in filter systems, is used as fuel, and is a catalyst for chemical reactions.

uranium.description: An extremely dense energy source. Emits deadly radiation in its raw form. Can only be transported with special equipment. The core of the nuclear reactor.

hydrogen.description: The lightest element in the universe. Produces efficient energy in fuel cells but carries an explosion risk when compressed. Storage infrastructure is mandatory.

silicon.description: The basic component of glass and solar panels. Also plays a critical role in electronic circuits. Easily obtained from sand and rocks.

quartz.description: Required for producing optically pure glass. Irreplaceable by silicon in observation modules and laser systems.

limestone.description: The raw material for concrete and construction materials. Consumed in large quantities during base expansion operations. Abundantly found in surface layers.

sulfur.description: Used in fertilizer production and chemical processes. Burning it releases toxic SO₂ gas; ventilation is mandatory in enclosed spaces.

phosphorus.description: An indispensable mineral for plant growth. Nourishes the soil in enclosed farming systems. Strategic reserves should be kept for long-term colonies.

nitrogen.description: The inert gas that makes up the majority of the atmosphere. Used as fertilizer in farming systems. Mixed with oxygen systems when compressed; pure nitrogen is deadly if inhaled.
